image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) floating on dark water. The duck features a characteristic iridescent green head, a white neck ring, a chestnut breast, and a grey/white body with black tail feathers. One orange webbed foot is visible paddling underwater. The background is dark, rippled water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and yellow-green in color, matching the description perfectly.
The eye is visible on the side of the head and appears dark/black.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is consistent with a swimming duck, appearing streamlined and floating correctly on the water surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The plumage matches the specific Mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey/white flanks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One orange leg/foot is visible beneath the water surface. While partially obscured by refraction, the webbed structure and orange color are consistent with a duck's anatomy.
The folded wing is visible on the side of the body, showing proper feather layering and shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear, showing the characteristic upward curl of the central black feathers typical of male mallards.
